correctness.rationale: Full support and bounded iid Hoeffding decomposition make long-run variance a sum of four nonnegative squared norms. Its zero set is exactly adjacent-pair coboundaries. Triple pattern constancy forces all edge-diagonal values equal when three ordered alphabet symbols exist; this leaves exactly normalization and two ascent/descent telescoping contrasts. With two symbols, the four values of an edge potential modulo constants plus the mean give four independent null functions among seven supported patterns. Single-symbol patterns are deterministic. Stationary two-dependence gives the covariance limit and multivariate CLT. Exact-rational joint indicator calculations at lags zero through two, performed from the actual standalone verifier, passed nine complete matrices for q=1,2,3,4. No finite census is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The indexed primary 2023 article specifies thirteen weak-order patterns and null pattern probabilities, and its accessible Proposition 3.1 addresses the three pair-comparison patterns for windows of length two; its presented tests use resampling rather than a full explicit covariance-rank classification for 13 length-three patterns. The 2024 arXiv full text presents generalized ordinal definitions and distributional limit theory without a complete full weak-order covariance nullspace. Bandt 2022 treats six strict tie-free patterns for continuous iid observations and obtains a different rank-four null structure; that result cannot imply the binary/ternary discrete rank jump. The new claim proves a pattern-constant coboundary classification for positive-mass finite alphabets of every cardinality, including an additional binary-only contrast. Semantic published-finding corpus searches for the exact claim, aliases, coboundary reductions, and nearby finite-pattern results found no dominating record; lack of a hit does not prove global originality.

value.rationale: Generalized ordinal patterns with ties are an established nonparametric method for detecting dependence in discrete time series; naive use of all thirteen pattern counts overlooks strong algebraic degeneracy in their asymptotic covariance. The theorem gives the exact effective dimension for every positive finite-alphabet law, even with highly unequal category masses, and identifies a genuine support-size phase transition at three categories. It fixes degrees of freedom for specified-null singular Gaussian quadratic statistics and reveals the extra binary-only telescoping identity, which is not evident from the marginal pattern distribution or a finite numeric covariance example. The result is structural and not a routine numerical recomputation.
